documents.name: Discharge Summary.txt
chunks: Patient is a 58-year-old male admitted for evaluation of poorly controlled blood glucose and fatigue over the preceding three weeks.
Primary diagnosis on this admission is Type 2 diabetes mellitus with secondary hypertension. No evidence of diabetic ketoacidosis on presentation.
Most recent laboratory results show an HbA1c of 8.2 percent, fasting glucose of 168 mg/dL, and an LDL cholesterol of 134 mg/dL.
On discharge the patient was started on metformin 500 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg once daily for blood pressure control.
Blood pressure at discharge was 148/92 mmHg. The patient was counseled on dietary changes and home glucose monitoring.
Follow-up with the primary care physician was scheduled in two weeks, with repeat HbA1c and a basic metabolic panel ordered at that visit.

documents.name: Chest Xray Report.txt
chunks: Examination: PA and lateral chest radiograph performed for evaluation of cough and shortness of breath.
The lungs are clear without focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. The cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits.
Impression: No acute cardiopulmonary process. No radiographic evidence of pneumonia at this time.

documents.name: Lab Panel.txt
chunks: Complete blood count: hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL, white blood cell count 7.4 thousand per microliter, platelets 245 thousand per microliter.
Basic metabolic panel: sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, and creatinine 1.1 mg/dL indicating preserved renal function.
Liver function tests were within normal limits with ALT 28 U/L and AST 24 U/L.
